# How to Improve Simulation-to-Real Performance for High-Dynamic Skills – Real vs. Simulated Differences?

> **Current answer:** In the G1 and cross-simulator settings of the ASAP report, small delta actions are learned as target physics trajectories and frozen in the training simulation to fine-tune the main policy. This approach reduces long-term dynamics and action tracking errors compared to SysID, delta dynamics, and uniform action noise. The residual model is only valid within its collected version/operating condition, and the issue has been reported alongside thermal damage to two robots.

## Credibility and review status

- **Handbook level:** `L3 Reviewed engineering conclusion`

- **Confidence:** `0.78`
- **Confidence rationale:** Two cross-simulator benchmarks, real tracking comparisons, extensive ablations and public code support the mechanism. Confidence is capped by only two representative real quantitative motions and a 4-DoF rather than full-body real delta model.

## Assumptions

- Representative target-physics state/action trajectories can be collected and synchronized.
- The residual model is revalidated for the robot, firmware, load and thermal state.

## Diagnosis and verification

- First verify the applicable robot, simulator, controller, environment, and assumptions, then follow the evidence locators below to inspect the original experiment or implementation.

## Result

- In the G1 and cross-simulator settings of the ASAP report, small delta actions are learned as target physics trajectories and frozen in the training simulation to fine-tune the main policy. This approach reduces long-term dynamics and action tracking errors compared to SysID, delta dynamics, and uniform action noise. The residual model is only valid within its collected version/operating condition, and the issue has been reported alongside thermal damage to two robots.

## Limitations

- Representative target-physics state/action trajectories can be collected and synchronized.
- The residual model is revalidated for the robot, firmware, load and thermal state.

## Safety notes

- **Validated in simulation:** Yes
- **Command limits:** Derive robot/firmware-specific joint position, velocity, torque, current, temperature and task-energy envelopes; paper jump and gain settings are not deployment limits.
- **Emergency stop:** Test an independent emergency stop and safe power-removal behavior before dynamic data collection.
- **Protective controls:** Use fall arrest or padded capture where compatible, an exclusion zone, thermal/current monitoring, inspection intervals and a dedicated safety operator.
- **Robot-specific warning:** The real delta model covers four G1 ankle DoFs under the reported setup; other joints, robots, firmware, payloads or wear states require recollection and review.
- **Staged deployment:** Validate target-dynamics replay in simulation, then low-energy supported motions, locomotion, partial dynamic skills and only then bounded agile actions with abort thresholds.

## Evidence

- [ASAP: Aligning Simulation and Real-World Physics for Learning Agile Humanoid Whole-Body Skills](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.01143v3>) — `support/primary`; Figures 2, 4-5, 10-12 and Tables III-V; Defines the delta-action alignment and compares SysID, delta dynamics, noise and fine-tuning choices.
- [LeCAR-Lab/ASAP official implementation](<https://github.com/LeCAR-Lab/ASAP/tree/df5320cc47dd8cad97961bdfabfe402dd62ad999>) — `support/primary`; DeltaA_OpenLoop._compute_torques, DeltaA_ClosedLoop._compute_torques and PPODeltaA._rollout_step at df5320c; Maps the residual and policy fine-tuning mechanism to official code.
